# AI Engineering Compiler v0.4.0

0.3.1 made the `spec-driven` commit guard hard to walk around. This release
compiles the fence around it, and adds a way to check that the fence is there.

## Permissions and sandbox, compiled

```yaml
permissions:
  deny: ["Read(.env)", "Read(./.env.*)"]
sandbox:
  enabled: true
```

Both blocks work in a manifest or a blueprint and merge into
`.claude/settings.json` under the same ownership rules as hooks. An entry you
already had is never claimed, a value you set is never overwritten
(`settings-value-conflict`), and a hand edit to an entry the compiler owns
stops the sync (`settings-entry-modified`). A rule in both lists is denied.

Codex and Cursor cannot enforce either block, and now say so on every run as a
warning, so `--strict` fails rather than letting a deny rule hold in one tool
and not another.

## The guard protects itself

The `spec-driven` pack (now version 3) denies the agent edits to
`.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.claude/hooks/`, and
`.ai/generated/` — the hook, the entry that runs it, and the local file that
could set `disableAllHooks`. Opt out with
`disable: [permission.protect-guardrails]`.

## `aie audit`

`aie check` proves generated files match their source. `aie audit` asks whether
that source describes a defended repository: an empty deny list, the sandbox
off, `enableAllProjectMcpServers`, secrets no `Read` rule covers, `--no-verify`
left open, hooks that match `"git commit"` as a substring, and a guard hook with
no CI check behind it. Each finding has a stable code and a fix. It reads
secret files by name, never their contents.

The GitHub Action runs it. The new `audit` input defaults to `warn`, which
annotates findings without failing your pipeline; set `audit: fail` to enforce.

## A threat model

[`docs/threat-model.md`](../../docs/threat-model.md) states what each layer —
rules, permissions, hooks, sandbox, CI — stops, what it does not, and where it
can be walked around, with each claim tied to a test or to Claude Code's
documentation.

## Upgrading

- **The `ai` command is gone.** Use `aie`; arguments, flags, and exit codes are
  unchanged. Do not switch to `npx ai` — on npm that is an unrelated package.
- **Blueprint users:** run `aie sync`. The pack's new deny rules land in
  `.claude/settings.json`, and `aie check` reports drift until you sync.
